Theorem 4.2. For a connected quiver setting (Q, d), the representation space Ra (Q) is a spherical variety under the action of Ba C Ga if and only if (Q, d) is a thin connect sum of quiver settings with Q of the form 1 « 2 « 3, and d = (m, n, 1) or d = (m, 2, n). Proof. First assume Ra(Q) is spherical. We reduce to the claimed situation in several steps, always using the previous lemma. (1) If Q contains a cycle, then Ra(Q) even admits infinitely many Ga-orbits, since there are already infinitely many isomorphism classes of representations of dimension vector (1,...,1) for any cycle quiver. Thus we can assume Q to be a tree.
